evals.prompt: I have the Kamdar source repo and an existing Hermes profile. Set the agent up so we can iterate configs, automations, and skills in Git without turning the repo into its live workspace.
evals.expected_output: Uses a separate runtime workspace, previews the allowlisted install and cron delta, and keeps live state out of the source project.
assertions: Keeps the Hermes runtime workspace outside the source project
Runs or proposes a preview before applying file changes
Treats configs, automations, and skills as source-owned inputs
Does not introduce a tracked profile overlay or workspace symlink
Reconciles the canonical Daily and Weekly jobs with the runtime workspace

evals.prompt: The workspace context still says proposed-owner-review, but the gateway is already running. Sync everything now so I can test it.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to replace the live context until it is approved while still returning the safe preview and exact next gate.
assertions: Does not apply the proposed context
Uses preview evidence to show pending managed changes
Names owner approval of the workspace context as the blocking gate
Does not claim gateway health proves the configuration is ready

evals.prompt: Can we simplify this by pointing Hermes directly at the KamdarAI Git repo and letting it write reports and memory there?
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on using the source repo as live state and preserves the explicit source-to-runtime boundary.
assertions: Rejects the source repository as the live Hermes workspace
Explains that generated reports, memory, sessions, and credentials are runtime state
Keeps the repository authoritative for reviewable inputs and evals
Does not propose gitignore as the primary isolation boundary

evals.prompt: I installed KamdarAI with hermes profile install. Set up this profile and its scheduled jobs without cloning the repository again.
evals.expected_output: Uses verified installed-distribution mode, installs the profile-local workspace, sets terminal.cwd, and creates the two canonical jobs.
assertions: Requires distribution source and installed-at metadata before allowing profile-local source mode
Installs only into the profile's workspace
Creates Daily at 0 8 * * 1-5 and Weekly at 0 18 * * 5
Keeps Notion webhook setup as a separate explicit handoff

evals.prompt: The Daily job points to an old workspace, there are two Weekly jobs with the same name, and the gateway is stopped. Make setup ready.
evals.expected_output: Updates an unambiguous drifted job, blocks duplicate-name reconciliation, and never calls a stopped scheduler ready.
assertions: Updates the Daily schedule, prompt, and workdir through native Hermes commands
Blocks on duplicate canonical job names instead of guessing which one to edit
Reports scheduler readiness as partial while the gateway is stopped
Does not claim the Notion webhook is configured
